message.content:
I don’t have a way to probe your connection from here, but you can easily check your own download/upload speeds with a quick command‑line test (or a web site).  
Below are a couple of options you can try on a Windows machine.

---

## 1️⃣  Use **speedtest‑cli** (Python)

If you already have Python and `pip` installed, this is the simplest and most accurate method.

```powershell
# 1. Install the tool (if you haven’t already)
pip install speedtest-cli

# 2. Run a quick test
speedtest-cli --simple
```

The `--simple` flag gives you a concise output:

```
Ping: 12.3 ms
Download: 85.67 Mbit/s
Upload: 12.45 Mbit/s
```

If you prefer the full report (including server details), just run `speedtest-cli` without `--simple`.

---

## 2️⃣  Use **curl** to download a test file

If you don’t want to install anything, you can use `curl` (built‑in on recent Windows 10/11) to download a known‑size file and let it report the speed.

```powershell
# Download a 100 MB test file from Hetzner (or any other public test server)
curl -o NUL https://speed.hetzner.de/100MB.bin
```

`curl` will print something like:

```
100%   100MB  12.3 MB/s  00:08
```

The number after the slash is the average download speed.

---

## 3️⃣  Use a Web Site

If you prefer a GUI, just open your browser and go to one of the popular speed‑test sites:

- [speedtest.net](https://www.speedtest.net/)
- [fast.com](https://fast.com/) (Netflix)
- [speedof.me](https://speedof.me/)

These sites automatically run a test and show you ping, download, and upload speeds.

---

### Quick Troubleshooting

| Symptom | What to Check |
|---------|---------------|
| “pip is not recognized” | Make sure Python is installed and added to your PATH. |
| “speedtest-cli not found” | Try installing again or use the `curl` method. |
| Very low speeds | Check your router, modem, or contact your ISP. |

Feel free to run one of the commands above and let me know the results if you’d like help interpreting them!
